statement.p: Two particles are traveling through space. At time t the first particle is at the point (-2 + 3 t, -4 + t, -5 + 3 t) and the second particle is at (-18 - t, -20 - 3 t, -21 - t)
Describe the two paths in words. Then determine if the two particles collide, cross, or neither cross nor collide to fill in the following.

We see that
?
the paths cross, and the particles collide there
the paths of the particles cross, but with no collision
neither of these is true .
If they collide or their paths cross, indicate where (if neither is true, enter none).
A collision or crossing occurs at (x,y,z) = .

p.m: \text{the paths cross, and the particles collide there}

static.solution:
(-2,-4,-5) in the direction of the vector 3 \vec i + \vec j + 3 \vec k and the second passes through (-18,-20,-21) in the direction of the vector - \vec i - 3 \vec j - \vec k. The two paths are not parallel.
Is there a time t when the two particles are at the same place at the same time? If so, then the particles collide, and their coordinates will be the same. Equating coordinates, we get -2 + 3 t = -18 - t, \quad -4 + t = -20 - 3 t,\quad -5 + 3 t = -21 - t.
Since all three equations are solved by t=-4, the two particles do in fact arrive at the same place at the same time, and so they do collide.
Then, the two paths cross if there are times t_1 and t_2 such that the position of the first particle at time t_1 is the same as the position of the second particle at time t_2. In this case this is obvious: when t_1 = t_2 = -4, the paths cross.
